claims.name: task_success_rate
claims.definition: Episodes terminating SUCCESS divided by episodes measured. SUCCESS means the submitted SQL passed single-database execution accuracy against gold.

claims.name: execute_sql_error_rate
claims.definition: Failed execute_sql TOOL CALLS divided by total execute_sql TOOL CALLS. Tool-call denominator, not episodes. Distinct from the SQL_ERROR termination reason, which is episode-level.

claims.name: sql_error_terminations
claims.definition: Episodes whose FINAL SUBMITTED query failed to execute. Episode denominator. Not to be reported alongside the tool-call error rate.

claims.name: mean_model_turns_per_successful_task
claims.definition: Model API calls per successful episode. This is what max_steps caps.

claims.name: median_model_turns_per_successful_task
claims.definition: Median model API calls per successful episode.

claims.name: mean_tool_calls_per_successful_task
claims.definition: Tool invocations per successful episode, counting inspect_schema, execute_sql, and the single terminating submit_answer.

claims.name: mean_trajectory_records_per_successful_task
claims.definition: Rows written to steps.jsonl per successful episode = model turns + tool calls. This is the quantity previously published as 'steps', which was ambiguous.
claims.note: Superseded the ambiguous 'mean steps per successful task'.

claims.name: trajectory_step_records
claims.definition: Total rows in steps.jsonl across the run.

claims.name: indexed_spans
claims.definition: OTel span documents in Elasticsearch carrying attributes.run.id == this run. Exceeds trajectory records because spans also cover eval.run, agent.episode, sqlite.query, and verifier.execution, none of which are trajectory step rows.

claims.name: benchmark_only_estimated_cost_usd
claims.definition: Sum of per-episode estimated cost for THIS run only. Estimated from published list price, not billed.

claims.name: estimated_cost_per_episode_usd
claims.definition: Benchmark-only estimated cost divided by episodes measured.

claims.name: estimated_cost_per_successful_episode_usd
claims.definition: TOTAL benchmark estimated cost divided by the number of successful episodes. Includes spend on failed episodes, because those were paid for too. Not the mean cost of a successful episode.

claims.name: mean_cost_of_a_successful_episode_usd
claims.definition: Mean estimated cost of episodes that succeeded, excluding spend on failures. Reported only to keep it distinguishable from the canonical cost-per-success above; do not publish it as cost per success.

claims.name: total_input_tokens
claims.definition: Prompt tokens reported by the API, summed over the run.

claims.name: total_output_tokens
claims.definition: Completion tokens reported by the API, summed over the run.

claims.name: gold_pass_qa
claims.definition: Gold queries fed to the evaluator as if they were predictions, and passing. Run before any agent episode; empty exclusion list follows.

claims.name: known_bad_detected
claims.definition: Deliberately wrong queries correctly rejected, among mutations that were FIRST PROVEN to return different rows from gold.

claims.name: mutation_execution_collisions
claims.definition: Mutations that changed the SQL text but returned exactly gold's rows on the shipped database, so they were discarded rather than counted as verifier leaks.

claims.name: mutation_collision_rate
claims.definition: Collisions divided by mutations ATTEMPTED. A property of this mutation set on this database. It is NOT an estimate of the share of the agent's passes that are false positives - the agent's queries are not drawn from this mutation distribution.

claims.name: max_step_episodes
claims.definition: Episodes terminating MAX_STEPS (model-turn cap reached without submitting).

claims.name: empty_result_loop_broad
claims.definition: Episode terminated MAX_STEPS AND executed at least one execute_sql call that returned row_count == 0 with error == None (a valid query returning no rows).

claims.name: abandoned_a_correct_query
claims.definition: Episode terminated MAX_STEPS AND at least one query it executed during the episode passes the official evaluator against gold. Established by re-running each executed query through verify_sql, not by inspection.

claims.name: repeat_pass_to_pass
claims.definition: Tasks with outcome pass to pass between spider_full__p0_v1 and spider_full__p0_v2, joined on task_id. PASS means termination_reason == SUCCESS.

claims.name: repeat_pass_to_fail
claims.definition: Tasks with outcome pass to fail between spider_full__p0_v1 and spider_full__p0_v2, joined on task_id. PASS means termination_reason == SUCCESS.

claims.name: repeat_fail_to_pass
claims.definition: Tasks with outcome fail to pass between spider_full__p0_v1 and spider_full__p0_v2, joined on task_id. PASS means termination_reason == SUCCESS.

claims.name: repeat_fail_to_fail
claims.definition: Tasks with outcome fail to fail between spider_full__p0_v1 and spider_full__p0_v2, joined on task_id. PASS means termination_reason == SUCCESS.

claims.name: repeat_total_pass_fail_flips
claims.definition: PASS->FAIL + FAIL->PASS across two runs of an identical recorded configuration. NOT the count of termination-reason changes, which is larger because it includes fail-to-fail reason changes.
claims.note: Supersedes an earlier figure of 49, which counted reason changes.

claims.name: repeat_termination_reason_changes
claims.definition: Any change in termination_reason between the two runs, including fail-to-fail changes that did not alter the outcome.

claims.name: abandoned_correct_query_in_empty_result_cohort
claims.definition: Exact intersection of episodes that abandoned a verifier-passing query with the empty_result_loop_broad cohort.

claims.name: abandoned_correct_query_share_of_benchmark_pp
claims.definition: Observed theoretical headroom in percentage points: episodes that executed a verifier-passing query and never submitted it, over all measured episodes. NOT guaranteed recoverable accuracy.

claims.name: p0_criteria_verified
claims.definition: P0 completion criteria passing in scripts/verify_p0_completion.py.

cost_ledger.pricing_basis: Published list price at time of run. NOT a billed invoice amount. Cached-input pricing is applied when the API reports cached prompt tokens, so recomputing cost from headline input/output prices alone yields a slightly higher figure.
